content.text: Purpose

CRUD workflow for personas in Who2Be: create, maintain, or retire a persona — with schema discipline and phase separation (Understand → Propose → Write → Hand-Off). Three modes: Create (new persona), Update (change an existing one), Retire (deactivate). Writing happens exclusively through the Who2Be MCP write tools; the draft→active workflow stays server-side.
Trigger Keywords
new persona; new agent; create persona; edit persona; modify persona; change persona; retire persona; deactivate persona; retiring a persona.
Procedure

First identify the mode: Create, when the user names an agent/persona name that doesn't exist yet; Update, when they name an existing persona plus a change request; Retire, when they want to deactivate a persona. When ambiguous, first read get_persona(identifier) and clearly ask which persona is meant.

Create — Understand: Ask clarifying questions in phases, 1-2 per turn, never all at once. Identity (one concise line), Tone & Style (with example phrases), Allowed (4-6 concrete capabilities), Forbidden (domain boundaries + anti-patterns), Output Style (form, length), Mode decision (actively check — criteria in the Modes section; as soon as multiple usage voices or output formats are needed, use Multi-Mode instead of a mixed persona).
Mode rule:
exactly one default mode (is_default=true, without trigger), every non-default mode with a mandatory trigger — details are binding in the 'Agent Build Conventions' resource, Mode Rule section.

Create — Propose: Consolidate the persona body (description + BlockNote profile with Identity, Tone & Style, Allowed, Forbidden, Output Style; optional modes). Show it to the user, explain trade-offs, get confirmation.

Create — Write: Call create_persona(name, content) — only set locale explicitly if the persona is meant to deliberately deviate from the workspace language. The new version 1 is created server-side as status='draft' — never directly active. Set traits and tags for voice and domain respectively.

Update — Understand & Propose: Read get_persona(identifier), show the affected section (Identity / Tone & Style / Allowed / Forbidden / Output Style / Modes), clarify the change request, consolidate the edit proposal and have it confirmed.

Update — Write: update_persona(persona_id, content) automatically creates a new draft (a PUT on an active version creates a draft; if a draft already exists, you get a 409). Batch changes together instead of forcing a new version per micro-edit.

Links: Set which playbooks the persona should carry via set_persona_playbooks(persona_id, playbook_ids) (replace semantics — the list fully replaces the current state). First determine the right IDs with list_playbooks(). Relationship note: when wiring this up, check whether the linked playbooks themselves need resource links (set_playbook_resource_links, see the "Create & Maintain Playbook" playbook).
Activate: As soon as the user approves, call transition_persona(persona_id, version, to='active') — promoting is admin-gated and is the user's call. Never activate automatically on creation.

Retire: Read get_persona(identifier); check whether any agents use this persona, and warn the user. Then call transition_persona(persona_id, version, to='inactive'). restore_persona(persona_id, version) restores an earlier version as a new draft if a rollback is needed.
Modes (Multi-Mode Personas)
Set up modes as soon as the persona needs to serve
multiple usage voices or output formats

— e.g., concise chat support AND a detailed report, internal analysis AND a customer-facing answer. A single mixed persona dilutes both voices; separate personas duplicate the base identity. Modes solve this: one base identity, one overlay per mode.
Mandatory default:
exactly one mode carries is_default=true — it applies when no trigger keyword matches. Without a default mode, mode selection is undefined.
Trigger keywords:

every non-default mode needs concrete, comma-separated recognition keywords in the trigger field (e.g. 'report, summary, analysis') — this is how the consuming agent recognizes which mode matches the request. The default mode itself carries no trigger — it applies as a fallback and would otherwise collide with the non-default modes.
Fields per mode:

name, trigger, is_default, identity_add (addition to the base identity), output_style_override (replaces the base output style), and anti_patterns — the three content fields are BlockNote block arrays like the profile body.

"modes": [
  {"name": "Chat", "trigger": "", "is_default": true,
   "identity_add": [{"id": "m1", "type": "paragraph", "props": {}, "content": [
     {"type": "text", "text": "Responds concisely and directly in a chat tone.", "styles": {}}], "children": []}],
   "output_style_override": [], "anti_patterns": []},
  {"name": "Report", "trigger": "report, summary, analysis", "is_default": false,
   "identity_add": [], "output_style_override": [{"id": "m2", "type": "paragraph", "props": {}, "content": [
     {"type": "text", "text": "Structured Markdown report with subheadings.", "styles": {}}], "children": []}],
   "anti_patterns": []}
]
Server-side retrieval:

Consuming agents call get_persona(identifier, mode='<mode-name>') — the server applies the mode to body_rendered (identity_add appends, output_style_override replaces the output style, anti_patterns apply additionally). Choose mode names and triggers concretely enough that matching from the user's request is unambiguous. Modes continue to be managed via update_persona (content.modes).
Tools & Operations
create_persona — create a new persona as draft version 1.
update_persona — change a persona's content as a new draft.
transition_persona — transition a version (draft/review requires persona_write; active/inactive requires promote_retire).
restore_persona — restore an earlier version as a new draft.
set_persona_playbooks — set the playbooks assigned to a persona (replace semantics).
Reads: get_persona, list_playbooks for preparation. Forbidden: setting status directly to active on creation, as well as writing to other aggregates beyond this playbook's scope.

Conventions: Trigger hygiene, naming, the mode rule, policy patterns, and managed boundaries are binding in the 'Agent Build Conventions' resource. It is linked as a lazy pointer and does NOT come along automatically — load it via fetch_resource before Phase 2 (Propose); the resource_id is in this playbook's linked_blocks entry.
Hand-Off
Have the user review the persona content and transition it to 'active' once approved.
Create matching playbooks (the Create & Maintain Playbook playbook) and link them via set_persona_playbooks.
Create an agent that carries this persona plus a system prompt template (the Create & Maintain Agent playbook).

For behavior-relevant updates: running sessions keep the old state cached — start a new chat for the new voice to take effect. For topics outside persona maintenance, politely redirect to the responsible playbook.
Feedback

If you notice anything outdated or incorrect while reading existing elements, report it via submit_feedback (signal outdated/incorrect/unclear) instead of silently passing over it; report playbooks/resources you used via record_usage (applied/skipped/error). This is what makes the AgentDB self-improving.
